subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramp schedule for Aurelius Bio - next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@aureliusbio.com>, Tim Shaw <tim.shaw@aureliusbio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial reservation options & quick decision milestones

Hi Lina / Tim —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a short proposal and a capacity workbook with three recommended reservation structures tailored to your inference patterns and regulatory needs. High level: we focused on predictable latency for inference-heavy peaks (bio-data annotation and batch scoring) while keeping unit economics flexible during model experimentation.

Summary of options in the proposal (attached):

- Option Alpha (Conservative): 8 GPUs reserved (4 long-lived lanes x 2 GPUs), can handle sustained low-latency scoring at 2k tokens/sec aggregate. Ramp: 60 days to full activation; includes 10% warmup credits for first 30 days.
- Option Beta (Balanced): 24 GPUs reserved (3x 8-GPU pools, two pools hot, one warm), supports burst windows and higher throughput for ensemble model runs. Ramp: 30-day activation with a staged warmup cadence. Includes automated prefix caching and a soft-fallback policy to a lower-cost quantized variant.
- Option Gamma (Aggressive): 48 GPUs reserved (dedicated slate for model training-adjacent inference), immediate activation with capacity buffer but higher monthly commit. Ramp: 7-day activation with canary lanes and a 15% early-burn credit to offset ramping cost.

We also outlined a hybrid fallback (hosted overflow) and an SLA exception window for initial 90 days while traffic patterns stabilize.

Next steps I propose:
1) Please review the attached PDF and workbook and mark a preferred option.
2) If you choose Beta or Gamma, confirm the target go-live week so we can book prewarm slots in our pool.
3) If you have procurement constraints, Monica is copied to start the contract/redline path.

I'll follow up tomorrow with a short spreadsheet showing expected token-level cost for each option based on the sample workload you provided.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelius_Reservation_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), capacity_model_aurelius.xlsx (workbook)

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for this — the deck is clear and the workbook is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our infra and procurement teams before we commit:

1) For Option Beta, can you confirm the minimum sustained GPU allocation during non-peak hours? We want to avoid a minimum that blocks overnight batch jobs.
2) What does the canary process look like in Option Gamma? Specifically: number of canary lanes, rollback timeline, and whether we can pin the canary to a single region.
3) Are the warmup credits refundable if we shorten the ramp after activation? Our CFO prefers credits applied to future invoices rather than one-time rebates.

Also, procurement asked whether there is a 30-day escape hatch (decommit with limited penalty) if the usage baseline diverges materially from the forecast.

Cc'ing our engineering lead Tim for any technical nuance.

Best,
Lina Ortega
VP, ML Ops
Aurelius Bioinformatics

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the quick review and great questions. Answers inline: 

1) Option Beta minimum: we recommend a 2-GPU soft-floor per warm pool (meaning you keep 2 GPUs warm per pool during low hours). That supports small overnight batches while allowing autoscaling for burst windows. We can make that a configurable soft-floor (no hard penalty) if you prefer.

2) Option Gamma canary: we usually run 2 canary lanes (each 1/16 of the slate), run for 48 hours, and observe tail-latency and token cost. Rollback policy: automatic reroute to Beta-equivalent pools within 15 minutes on SLA breach. Yes — canaries can be pinned to a single region (we'll reserve the GPUs in us-west-2 if you want).

3) Warmup credits: we apply them as invoice credits by default (not one-time rebates). If you shorten the ramp, the remaining credits are retained as account credits for 12 months.

Escape hatch: we can offer a 30-day partial decommit for the first year with a stepping penalty (first 30 days notice = 10% of remaining monthly commit, 31-60 days = 25%). We outlined this as an optional addendum in the PDF.

I'll loop Karthik for a brief sizing note on memory/sequence expectations so you get realistic min-GPU numbers for metric-heavy model runs. Monica will pick up contracting.

-- Priyom

Subject: Re: Initial reservation options & quick decision milestones — technical sizing note

Hi all —

Quick technical sizing guidance based on Lina's sample workload (70% chat-like interactions at median 512 tokens, 30% batch scoring at 8k tokens):

- Effective tokens/sec estimates: baseline concurrent workload maps to ~18k tokens/sec aggregate.
- Memory/kv-cache: ensemble runs with 3-way models need 45GB of model RAM headroom per GPU for the quantized variant; unquantized variants require ~72GB. That implies that Option Alpha (8 GPUs) in unquantized mode will saturate for long-context batch jobs; recommend quantized or Beta/ Gamma for heavy batch windows.

Min-GPU recommendations:
- Overnight baseline (low traffic): 4 total GPUs in quantized single-model mode for safe overnight batch completion.
- Daytime baseline: 12 GPUs (Beta-equivalent) to keep p95 latency under 300ms for chat workloads.

Operational notes: canary lanes should run the exact model revs and a shared prompt set for at least 24 hours with end-to-end tracing enabled (we'll provide the tracing hooks). For region pinning: please confirm whether your data residency requires an EU region; otherwise we'll provision in us-west-2 as discussed.

-Karthik
Lead, Serving Performance
Redwood Inference
